match.reason: The closest bank point, What liveability means, defines liveability in general terms and does not teach how specific human factors such as crime, traffic, pollution, noise, housing costs and jobs influence it, so it is broader than the new point.

draft.title: Human influences on liveability
card: Human influences on liveability come from what people do and build, not from nature. They can make a place more or less pleasant, safe and affordable to live in.
Crime, traffic, pollution and noise can lower liveability. People may feel less safe, breathe dirtier air, lose sleep or spend longer getting around.
Housing costs matter too. When rent and house prices are high, fewer people can afford to live in a place, even if it is pleasant.
Job opportunities can raise liveability, because people can earn an income close to home. Few jobs can lower it, as people may have to travel far or move away.
draft.remember: Human influences are what people do and build: crime, traffic, pollution, noise, housing costs and jobs.

a.q: Which of these is a human influence on liveability?
opts: Heavy traffic on the main road through a town
A river that floods after heavy rain
A hot and dry climate in summer
A steep hill that makes building hard
a.why: Traffic comes from what people do and build, so it is a human influence. The flood, the climate and the hill are features of nature, so they are not human influences. Nature shapes them, not people.
a.clue: Which one is caused by people, not by nature?

b.q: Few businesses in Narrabri's town centre have opened in recent years, and many young people leave to find work. Which human influence is lowering liveability?
opts: Limited job opportunities
High levels of traffic noise
Rising air pollution
High rates of crime
b.why: Few jobs lead people to move away to find work, so limited job opportunities are the human influence here. Noise, pollution and crime can lower liveability too, but the case does not mention them.
b.clue: Why would young people leave to find work?

a.best: Heavy traffic on the main road through a town
